title: The proportional distribution of training by elite endurance athletes at different intensities during different phases of the season
authors: Sperlich B, Matzka M, Holmberg HC
journal: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
population: 175 retrospective TIDs from elite-to-world-class endurance athletes across sports (120 HR-based)
findings: Of 175 TIDs, 89 were pyramidal, 65 polarized and 8 threshold; 49% were single-case studies, mostly cross-country skiing and biathlon.
In 91% (n=160) of TIDs more than 60% of endurance exercise was low intensity.

Triathlon, speed skating, rowing, running, cross-country skiing and biathlon had >80% in zone 1 and <12% in zone 2; cyclists and swimmers had a lower zone 1 share (16% quoted for the lower figure in the abstract).

For most athletes the heavy-to-severe share was higher in the competition period than the preparatory phase, but authors conclude the literature does not allow general conclusions because quantification methods vary widely.
limitations: Authors state the evidence base cannot support general TID prescriptions; heterogeneous methods; elite athletes only; many single-case studies.
implications: Treat every TID target as a prior with an uncertainty band: pyramidal is more common than polarized and threshold is rare.
Allow a higher high-intensity share in the competition phase than in the base phase, parameterised by event and athlete.
Keep TID type as a descriptive output of the plan, not an optimization target.

verification.notes: Crossref: online 2023-10-27. Counts confirmed in abstract. Grade B because the review is systematic but descriptive and heterogeneous.
